newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Mugabe's plane makes emergency landing in Ireland.
newsitem.headline: Mugabe's plane makes emergency landing in Ireland.

text.p: A plane carrying Zimbabwean President Robert Mugabe was forced to make an emergency landing at Ireland's Shannon airport on Monday night after an alert over a possible fire in an engine, airport officials said.

Mugabe, who had been in Ireland attending a conference on Africa, had to spend an unscheduled extra night in the country after his Air Zimbabwe Boeing 707 plane was forced to turn back. None of his 37-strong party was hurt but some were reported to be shaken by the incident.

Airport officials said the plane took off from Dublin and refuelled at Shannon, but shortly after takeoff a fire warning light came on. The plane remained air bound for an hour dumping fuel before landing at Shannon as a precaution.
Mugabe's press spokesman George Charamba told Reuters that some of the passengers thought they had seen sparks coming from an engine.
"As we were gaining height, some of the passengers claimed they noticed some kind of fire in the right engine," he said.
Charamba said Mugabe and his party spent the night in hotels near Shannon and were expected to leave for Harare on Tuesday.
